title: Audit event schema: compact diff encoding, redaction rules, and sampling strategy for RBAC v2 & SSO
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define a practical, compact audit event schema and an associated taxonomy for RBAC v2, SSO/SAML admin flows, and high-privilege admin controls. Deliverables: 1) canonical event shape used by services writing to the audit pipeline; 2) compact diff encoding for target state changes to minimize log size while keeping diffs machine-parseable and reviewable; 3) redaction and PII handling rules for identity-linked fields (SAML attributes, email, IP); 4) sampling and retention guidance for noisy endpoints; 5) rollout & migration plan with compatibility strategy for existing consumers (analytics, compliance).
rationale: Current audit payloads vary between services: some write entire resource snapshots, others ad-hoc key lists. With RBAC v2 introducing more granular role bindings and SSO/SAML adding federated identities, naive full snapshots blow up event size and increase cost. We need a consistent, compact, and privacy-aware format to support compliance audits, forensics, and automated alerting without over-indexing storage costs.
diff_encoding_choice: Selected format: ordered compact diff array using op tuples: [op, path, old_value, new_value]. Ops: 'M' (modify), 'A' (add), 'R' (remove), 'S' (salted-hash for large blob replacement). Rationale: predictable size, easy to stream-serialize, efficient for sparse changes like RBAC role binding updates.
diff_examples: Example 3: large policy replaced with salted-hash -> ["S", "/org/policy", "sha256:oldhash", "sha256:newhash"]
privacy_and_redaction: Principles: minimize PII in raw logs; preserve auditability. Rules: 1) identity fields (email, subject identifiers) are recorded as stable hashed identifiers 'uid:sha256:<salted>' and a separate identity-resolution table (access-controlled) maps hashes to real identities for compliance requests; 2) SAML attributes: store attribute names and hashed values unless explicit legal/compliance need is present; 3) IP addresses: truncate to /24 for IPv4 or /56 for IPv6 by default; 4) sensitive blobs (private keys, SAML assertions) must never be stored raw; replace with salted-hash marker via 'S' op in diffs; 5) redact tokens and secrets entirely. Operational note: redaction policy enforced at producer library (audit-sdk) with deterministic salt stored in KMS per-org for consistent hashing.
sampling_and_retention: Guidance: 1) Critical admin actions (role/grant/revoke, org-config changes, RBAC role creation/updation, SSO configuration changes) must be logged 100% and retained for 7 years for compliance customers. 2) Noisy read-only queries (role lookups, token introspects) sampled at 1% by default and kept 90 days. 3) High-frequency user-facing events (login success/failure) keep 100% for 90 days, then downsample to 5% for 2 years for trend analysis. 4) Sampling tags must be deterministic and indicated in event.meta.sampling to allow consumers to account for bias.
storage_and_indexing_strategy: Events are written to the audit Kafka topic with schema version header. Consumers: long-term archive (S3 Parquet via lake pipeline) and hot index (Elasticsearch/Opensearch) for recent 90 days. Indexing: index by tenant_id, event_type, actor_hash, target_type. Avoid indexing full diff payload; store compressed payload in object store and surface pointer in index. Ensure per-tenant encryption keys and RBAC to access archives.
backcompat_plan: Schema v2 introduces 'diff' field and 'actor_hash' normalized id. Producers will ship audit-sdk v2 that accepts both full 'snapshot' and 'diff' payloads and translates legacy snapshots into canonical diffs during ingestion. Ingestion service will support mixed-mode for 6 months with a compatibility flag. Migration tasks include updating 10 highest-volume services first, then gradual rollout to all services.
rollout_tasks: Create audit-sdk v2 with client-side redaction and deterministic hashing (Task owner: ENG-SEC-SDK)
Implement ingestion adapter that converts legacy snapshots to diffs (owner: infra-audit-team)
Add indexing change to Opensearch cluster to add actor_hash and tenant_id (owner: infra-search)
Update compliance runbook and data-access playbooks (owner: legal-compliance)
Ship migration PRs for 10 highest-volume services (list in links)
acceptance_criteria: Audit events for RBAC role changes are <= 30% of previous snapshot size on average for services that adopt diff encoding
Ingestion accepts both legacy snapshots and diff payloads and normalizes to canonical storage format
Redaction rules applied by audit-sdk eliminate raw PII fields in staged test logs (verified by privacy team)
Search queries for recent 90d events return actor and target pivots within SLA (500ms median)
Compliance team can reconstruct user-facing action timeline for a given uid_hash using archive mapping and identity resolution process

2025-03-07 - Priya Patel (Privacy): Agreed on salted hashing approach but requested that salt rotation plan be documented. Added todo to rollout_tasks.
2025-03-09 - Tomas Müller (Infra Search): Concern: indexing actor_hash will increase storage; suggested storing actor_hash as keyword only and offloading full actor resolution to a lookup service.
2025-03-11 - Security Review (notes): Approve diff encoding; require threat model on identity-resolution table access (must be audited and limited).
2025-03-12 - Luca Romano: Began implementation of audit-sdk changes; created first PR. Marking status as In Progress.
notes: Related work: tie into RBAC v2 rollout tasks to ensure role IDs are stable and globally unique. Ensure SSO/SAML attribute mapping in IDP connectors emits stable subject identifier for hashing. Plan a tabletop exercise with incident response to validate the format and retrieval workflows.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for diff encoding/decoding and roundtrip to snapshot converter; 2) Integration test writing to Kafka and verifying ingestion normalization; 3) Privacy test that verifies no cleartext PII emitted by services using audit-sdk v2; 4) Load test to measure event size reduction and ingestion throughput impact.
open_questions: How long should salted-hash mapping be retained in identity-resolution table before automatic purge? (privacy requested 1 year, compliance requests 7 years)
Should login IP be stored at full precision for security investigations or always truncated?
Do we need a per-customer override flag (legal_hold) to bypass redaction for customers with explicit consent and audit requirements?
